classification.difficultyReason: Quadrilateral angle sum in three variants. Part a gives the reflex interior angle directly. Part b requires converting an exterior marked angle to 360° minus it. Part c does the same conversion with an algebraic expression and solves a linear equation. The interpretation of the marked angle and the algebra make the hardest part a routine linked procedure. It is above the special-quadrilateral property lookups but without the parallelogram-and-straight-line chain of p42-q14.

content.prompt: Determine the size of the unknown angle in each quadrilateral.

answer.worked:
The $230^\circ$ reflex angle is an interior angle. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $130^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-130=230^\circ$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $(2a+30)^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-(2a+30)=330-2a$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+(330-2a)&=360\\410-a&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.
